digest.component_or_area: LLM verifier configuration and class resolution
propositions: Multiple independent code paths select the verifier model by comparing against a default, causing non-default models (Bedrock ids, provider-qualified ids) to silently bypass the downgrade and run on the frontier model instead.

Three verifier paths (plan_review/_verifier_cfg, completion.py equality test, code-review.yaml verify step) lack a unified mechanism to resolve the reserved class names (trivial/standard/frontier) through the operator's class configuration, so they either apply no downgrade or fall through to cfg.model.

code-review.yaml's verify step declares no model key and carries temperature:0 for greedy Pass-2 determinism, but that setting never takes effect because the step defaults to cfg.model (frontier), causing both the wrong model AND loss of the claimed determinism.

resolve_model_string must become the single vocabulary for reserved class names and be called from all four verifier call sites, with lazy imports to avoid circular dependencies between model_classes and config.

The solution replaces equality-test-based downgrades with a class-name indirection: expressing verifier choices via the standard/trivial/frontier class slot rather than comparing cfg.model to a constant.
